It costs engineering effort to instrument per-category token usage and to control for shared cached prefixes across concurrent runs, and it adds no new model or infrastructure dependency. It can fail if applied as a blanket conclusion: the negative results depend on a specific cache price ratio (one tenth of uncached) and on specific benchmarks, so a policy that loses money in this study may still pay off under different provider pricing, cache behavior, or task distributions, and shorter prompts can backfire by inducing more agent steps. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Multi-Agent Memory Inconsistency: Where Factual Conflicts Disappear in LLM Agents
item.description: This is a benchmark and evidence-flow profiler for diagnosing memory inconsistency in multi-agent LLM systems; it replaces informal assumptions that delegating retrieval to workers preserves the lead agent's ability to detect factual conflicts. It costs nothing in model capacity but adds evaluation instrumentation and logging of worker-to-lead evidence flow, and the operational implication is that handoff design or claim co-location must be engineered explicitly. Adoption can fail because the findings are measured on Harvey LAB document-review tasks with three models at matched generation spend, so the specific rates may not transfer to other domains, and fixing handoffs does not guarantee detection improves in a different pipeline. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: XM-Sparse: High-Throughput Sparse-Attention LLM Serving over Scale-up Memory Pools
item.description: XM-Sparse replaces PCIe-based host-memory KV offloading by aggressively offloading both the sparse KV cache and the indexer K-index cache to a scale-up memory pool, using TMA-fused tile-level retrieval for dynamic KV and GPU-initiated DMA prefetching for predictable index pages. It costs implementation complexity atop SGLang, access to scale-up memory expansion hardware, and the engineering burden of coordinating prefetch with latency-critical decode operations. It can fail if real (non-emulated) memory-pool bandwidth or latency diverges from the emulation, if access-pattern assumptions break for other models or workloads, or if hot KV buffers still bound HBM concurrency at extreme context lengths. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
item.description: The paper proposes treating physical trials, simulators, learned judges, and formal checks as the 'test suite' for robot and lab code, replacing ad hoc or absent verification of programs written by coding agents for physical actuators. The cost is the expense and potential unreliability of physical evidence: real-world trials are costly and slow, while cheaper substitutes (simulators, learned judges, traces) can be wrong or gameable under search, and building a physical continuous-integration pipeline requires ongoing maintenance of skill libraries and evaluation infrastructure. What can fail is verification drift: learned or simulated judges diverge from real-world behavior, so programs validated cheaply may fail on hardware or violate safety constraints that task success alone does not capture. 1 independent implementation, 3 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Harnesses That Improve Themselves: A Unifying Framework for Self-Improving Agent Harnesses
item.description: This replaces static, manually tuned agent harnesses and prompt-only reflection with a loop that diagnoses execution traces, patches one of four runtime components (context, control, tools, verification), and deploys changes only after validation gates. It costs additional inference for trace diagnosis and patch validation, plus engineering effort to build sandboxed candidate evaluation, though the paper claims lower token cost than full rewrites. It can fail through benchmark gaming, evaluator tampering, prompt bloat, and overfitting of self-modifications to one model or repository. 1 independent implementation, 23 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
item.description: The proposal would replace reliance on final code and passing tests as sole QA evidence with structured analysis of agent execution trajectories to prioritize consequential decisions for human scrutiny. The cost is instrumentation to capture trajectories, new analysis tooling, and additional reviewer effort, with no quantified benefit established. It can fail because trajectories do not establish that decisions were justified or corrective changes effective, and the added scrutiny may not outperform simpler existing QA approaches. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BQ-LoRA: Binary-Quantized Low-Rank Adapters as Implicit Regularizers for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
item.description: BQ-LoRA replaces the FP16 low-rank adapters used in QLoRA with 1-bit binarized adapters plus a learned per-layer scale and a Scaled Straight-Through Estimator, while keeping the 4-bit quantized base model unchanged. Training memory matches QLoRA and step time rises by under 4%, so the cost is implementation complexity and, for serving gains, dependence on a prototype extension of Punica's SGMV kernel; storage savings apply at inference and adapter-serving time only. The advantage is not uniform: on LLaMA-2 it loses to LoftQ at 7B and QLoRA at 70B, binarization with STE can be sensitive to scale and threshold initialization, and results rest on a single paper whose deployment kernel is a research prototype without production hardening. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers
item.description: InfuseLoop replaces the standard PLT loop recurrence, in which only the preceding in-trajectory hidden state crosses loop boundaries, with a cross-trajectory latent injection that aggregates causally available hidden states from later prediction trajectories via lightweight attention residuals. Costs are O(Rd) additional hidden-state storage, 0.3% decoding time over vanilla PLTs, and 23.3% over a non-looped baseline, while preserving token-parallel training and the vanilla PLT KV-cache footprint. It can fail if the reported stability and perplexity gains do not transfer beyond the paper's training scale, if looped-model decoding underutilizes the reader's single-GPU serving stack, or if integrating trajectory cross-dependencies complicates existing inference kernels. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning
item.description: The co-design replaces standard dense MPC rollouts over JEPA latent world models with reference-forest action sampling that manufactures differential bit-level sparsity, exploited by a purpose-built bit-exact accelerator. The cost is a custom hardware implementation plus a modified planner whose candidate sequences are coupled to shared roots, adding system complexity and constraining the sampling distribution. It can fail if real planning workloads lack the latent locality assumed, if the coupled sampling degrades planning quality on harder tasks, or if the custom accelerator is unavailable, since the reported speedups do not transfer to commodity GPUs. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DAQ: Decision-Aligned Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Transformers
item.description: DAQ replaces standard post-training quantization of spiking transformers with a decision-aligned calibration that keeps quantized membrane variables inside the floating-point model's firing regions along the quantized model's own trajectory. It requires only calibration data and no retraining, enabling 4-bit weights and membrane variables, but adds a state-trajectory-dependent calibration procedure more complex than generic PTQ. It can fail when firing decisions near decision boundaries diverge over recurrent time steps, and its energy benefits depend on spiking or neuromorphic deployment targets rather than conventional GPU inference. 2 independent implementations, 50 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HADVQ: Hessian Aware Directional Vector Quantization
item.description: HADVQ replaces scalar ultra-low-bit weight quantization (e.g., GPTQ-style per-channel rounding) with polar vector quantization using an E8-lattice codebook after random preconditioning, plus Hessian-proxy detection of sensitive channels preserved at higher precision for 0.16 extra bits. The cost is a complex offline quantization pipeline (preconditioning, polar decomposition, lattice codebook construction, Hessian estimation), non-standard decoding kernels that may lack mature inference-engine support, and a modest bit-rate increase for the protected channels. Failure modes include accuracy degradation if the proxy Hessian misidentifies important channels, latency regressions if lattice decoding is not efficiently implemented on the target GPU, and gains that may not transfer to models or calibration data distributions different from those evaluated. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models
item.description: LoopZip replaces full-length visual token sequences in looped (weight-shared) VLMs with a compressed set built from pre-backbone aggregation, cross-invocation attention-based token selection, and weight-tied value correction, all without additional training. It costs implementation complexity in the inference path and a small quality loss (about 2.8% at 50% pruning, degrading further at higher ratios), while saving roughly 58% peak GPU memory and about 2x latency. It can fail if the reader's production model is not a looped VLM, since the cross-invocation selection and value correction mechanisms assume shared layers called multiple times, and gains may not transfer to standard VLMs or workloads with few visual tokens. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LaFlash: Capacity-Driven Acceleration for Coding Agent Workflows via QLC-HBF
item.description: LaFlash replaces recomputation of evicted agent states (contexts and KV caches) with retention in a High-Bandwidth Flash tier built on QLC NAND, allocating memory between active concurrency and dormant-state storage via Session Grouping and Fast-Page Allocation. It requires specialized HBF hardware that does not exist in commodity GPU servers or API-based deployments, and its benefits depend on QLC's heterogeneous read latency and limited write endurance being managed through request-exclusive placement and HBM buffering. It can fail under highly irregular reactivation patterns that break read parallelism across session groups, or when write-intensive workloads exceed QLC endurance despite buffering. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LoopPrune: Recurrent Pruning for Looped Diffusion Transformers
item.description: LoopPrune replaces deploying a full dense looped diffusion Transformer with a structured-pruned version whose shared blocks are selected via recurrent importance estimation and recovered by distillation-style loop-position matching against a frozen dense teacher. The cost is an offline pruning-plus-recovery training phase requiring the teacher and data access, added pipeline complexity, and a residual quality gap (about 6.9% average accuracy loss at 30% pruning in the reported setting). It can fail if the target model is not a looped/shared-block architecture, if the recovery training is under-resourced, or if position-specific errors compound across recurrent iterations and degrade outputs beyond the reported benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SilverSpoon-KD: A General-Purpose Toolkit for Knowledge Distillation
item.description: SilverSpoon-KD replaces ad hoc or narrow distillation implementations with a single PyTorch API covering homogeneous, heterogeneous, quantization, and blockwise distillation across vision and language workloads. The cost is added toolkit dependency and integration complexity, plus the compute required to run teacher-student training, which on a single 24 GB GPU may require the blockwise mode or small teachers. Failure modes include student quality regressions relative to the teacher on domain-specific tasks, mismatched architectures limiting applicable distillation methods, and toolkit maturity risks typical of new open-source releases. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
item.description: WATERFALL replaces manual reward engineering and privileged-information reward shaping with automated discovery: persona-conditioned generation of programmatic reward candidates, evolutionary Swiss-system tournaments judged by vision-language models over raw visual rollouts, and iterative mutation and pruning of candidates. The cost is a full population-based RL pipeline—many parallel rollouts, repeated VLM inference for judging, and longitudinal tracking of candidate histories—far beyond a single-GPU setup and dependent on paid VLM API throughput. It can fail if VLM judgments are noisy or biased (selecting degenerate reward hacks), if the tournament converges prematurely on brittle rewards, or if discovered reward programs overfit the evaluation environments and do not transfer. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.
